author: Tim
title: Ashley Biden Shares Update On Father Joe Biden's Cancer Treatment
text:
Ashley Biden shared a heartfelt video showing her father, former president Joe Biden, finishing a round of radiation therapy at Penn Medicine. The clip showed him ringing the bell while surrounded by his wife Jill and their grandchildren, marking a moment of relief for the whole family.
Ashley’s post expressed how proud she was of her father’s strength and the care he received. Many people online responded with messages of love and support. Some said things like “Good to see this” and “He’s a fighter,” while others shared simple prayers for his recovery.
Cancer touches us all. Like so many of you, Jill and I have learned that we are strongest in the broken places. Thank you for lifting us up with love and support.
[pic.twitter.com/oSS1vGIiwU]— Joe Biden (@JoeBiden)
[May 19, 2025]
Not everyone reacted the same way though. A few people worried that his cancer might still return, while others commented on his appearance, joking about him wearing a full suit to the hospital. Still, most comments carried warmth and admiration, showing that many people were genuinely pulling for him.
Earlier in the year, it had been revealed that Joe was diagnosed with prostate cancer after tests showed a growth. His doctors explained that the cancer had spread to his bones but was hormone-sensitive, meaning it could still be managed effectively. He began treatment quietly with radiation and hormone therapy before the news became public.
Recently, more attention turned to his health when he was seen with stitches on his head after another surgery. A spokeswoman confirmed that Joe had Mohs surgery, which is a precise method used to remove skin cancer with minimal damage. It’s often used for cancers that return or appear on sensitive areas like the face or scalp.
Footage from a church visit showed Joe smiling and shaking hands, even as the scar on his head was clearly visible. Social media quickly noticed, with people asking questions and speculating about what had happened. Some showed concern, while others admired how strong and upbeat he looked despite the fresh wound.
The type of surgery he had, called Mohs, removes thin layers of skin one at a time until no cancer cells remain. It’s done under local anesthesia, and most people go home the same day. The procedure helps preserve healthy tissue while ensuring that the cancer is completely taken out.
Doctors explained that once the area is clear, the wound can be stitched, left open to heal, or repaired with nearby skin depending on its size. Patients are told to keep it covered for several days to help with healing and to avoid infection. Mild pain is normal afterward, though serious discomfort is rare and would mean a follow-up visit is needed.
Joe’s family has continued to stay close during this time, and Ashley’s post gave the public a rare and personal look into that support. Her words and the video seemed to remind people that behind all the politics, there’s still a family just hoping for their loved one to get better.
